about: A sign-in service you run yourself, giving many apps one shared login page and user list.

prs.title: Sign-in behind a Traefik proxy now ends on the right site
prs.broken: With the documented Traefik setup, people who signed in landed on the login service's own address instead of the app they had opened.
prs.changed: After sign-in the service now sends the browser to the app's own address with the same path, and still blocks redirects to other sites.
prs.matters: People end up back in the app they opened.

prs.title: Sign-in no longer breaks on special characters in the request
prs.broken: On the sign-in page, some values from the app asking for login were pasted into the request unchanged. A plus sign turned into a space, a hash mark cut the request short, and a lone percent sign made sign-in fail.
prs.changed: Every one of those values is now encoded before it is sent, on the sign-in, third-party callback and security key steps.
prs.matters: Apps get back the same values they sent, so sign-in works with any state or nonce.

prs.title: The service starts again with one common database setting
prs.broken: The settings let you name the small file-based database as "sqlite3". With that name the service crashed on startup, because one part still did not know it.
prs.changed: That part now treats "sqlite3" as the same database, the way the rest of the service already did.
prs.matters: People using that setting can start the service and sign in again.

prs.title: Signing out reaches every connected app again
prs.broken: When someone signs out, the service tells connected apps to sign them out too. For some security settings that message was never sent, or apps rejected it.
prs.changed: The sign-out message is now locked with the same method and key as the app's sign-in pass.
prs.matters: Signing out in one place signs you out of the connected apps, whichever security setting they use.

prs.title: Apps can sign in with a secret that has special characters
prs.broken: Apps that sent their ID and secret in the standard login header were turned away when the secret held characters like plus, slash or percent, even though the same secret worked another way.
prs.changed: The service now decodes the header values the way the standard says before comparing them.
prs.matters: Common client libraries work with any hand-set secret, not only the generated ones.
